messages:
alex: quick sync — i'm sketching a low-impact profiler plan we can safely run in prod. full nsys traces blow up latency. need ideas for sampling/guardrails that won't change kernel selection or cache behavior

mira: +1. TL;DR: use lightweight traces (NVTX + perfetto host timeline) for most samples, reserve full nsys/cupti for scheduled preprod runs. proposal: 0.5% sample rate, only on seq_len >= 512, cap trace window to 200ms, and never on Dedicated/Enterprise tenants. from dev runs: a full nsys capture bumped p99 ~2.5x; NVTX-only adds ~1-2% CPU and ~<5ms median extra latency on tiny requests.

sam: two things on KV cache & batching: 1) sampling can warm the cache / bias measurements if we probe hot keys. limit sampling to cold-prefixes or random hashes so we're not always touching the same tokens. 2) small-batch requests get over-represented in samples; weight sample selection by batch_size if we want representative kernel selection data.

derek: implementation sketch: runtime controlled via env + runtime flags. keep these simple and discoverable. e.g.
```
PROFILER_MODE=light        # off | light | full
PROFILER_SAMPLE_RATE=0.005
PROFILER_MIN_SEQ=512
PROFILER_MAX_MS=200
PROFILER_EXCLUDE_TIER=dedicated
```
light = NVTX marks + perfetto host trace; full = nsys/cupti for kernel timelines. light should stream traces to our secondary collector and write blobs to GCS asynchronously (not on hot path).

perf-bot: perf-bot: canary run (2026-03-10): 1k sampled reqs @0.8% -> avg overhead +3.2ms, median unaffected, tail +12ms for ~2% of traces. GPU busy-time +6% on sampled replicas; CPU sys time +1.6%. no errors.

mira: good data. add guardrails: auto-disable profiler if p99 delta > 5ms sustained for 5min, and backoff sample rate exponentially. add an opt-out header for high-value traffic (X-No-Trace: 1). redact prompts before persisting traces.

alex: also: make sure tracer instrumentation is non-invasive: NVTX + perfetto markers only annotate, avoid any syncs that force kernel timestamps. don't call any API that could change kernel selection heuristics (no artificial cache probes in production).

sam: another pattern: route sampled requests to a 'probe' replica set with identical model weights but lower batch_concurrency so we can capture kernel timelines without affecting main throughput. probe replicas should still service prod traffic but be limited in qps. this avoids perturbing the main batch allocator.

derek: note on telemetry: perfetto + NVTX gives host<->gpu alignment and kernel names via symbolization for most cases. for fine-grained kernel breakdown (fusion/aten ops) we still need occasional full nsys on preprod GPUs with identical drivers. schedule those monthly or on suspected regressions only.

alex: action items: mira -> RFC with rollout & revert thresholds + privacy redaction notes; derek -> add env controls + minimal light tracer impl (no CUPTI on light); sam -> design probe-replica routing and sampling weighting for batch sizes. i'll book a 30m canary window next wed.

mira: ok i'll draft the RFC today, will include the perf-bot numbers and recommended default sample=0.5% :+1:

derek: i'll prototype the env flags and async uploader this week.

sam: i'll write the probe-replica routing doc and examples for weighted sampling.

alex: thanks all. we'll follow up in the RFC thread. :rocket:
